recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It restores the applied Security WG clarification without undoing the later FHIR-32475 datatype expansion; no broader AuditEvent encoding policy change is indicated by the available Jira, source, git, Zulip, or Confluence evidence.
issue_request: FHIR-13759 was a Published Security WG change request for STU3, resolved Not Persuasive with Modification. It asked whether AuditEvent.entity.query and AuditEvent.entity.detail.value base64Binary content needed a fixed character encoding or a way to say how decoded bytes should be interpreted; the approved resolution was to add comments explaining event-specific meaning and secondary encoding rather than mandate a universal encoding.
initial_application: Git commit f36c03dbf21c applied Security update GF#13759 in the STU3-era AuditEvent spreadsheet source, adding the requested encoding comment to both AuditEvent.entity.query and AuditEvent.entity.detail.value. After source conversion, the query-side comment remains in source/auditevent/structuredefinition-AuditEvent.xml.
additional_context: AuditEvent is active in source/fhir.ini. FHIR-32475 later expanded AuditEvent.entity.detail.value[x] from string/base64Binary to the current choice of computable datatypes plus base64Binary, and commit bd6dd636238 removed the older FHIR-13759 detail-value comment while making that datatype change. FHIR-32475 did not reverse the base64Binary encoding clarification, and current source still allows valueBase64Binary.
reconciliation: Added a comment to source/auditevent/structuredefinition-AuditEvent.xml on AuditEvent.entity.detail.value[x], scoped to valueBase64Binary and updated for current element names by referencing AuditEvent.entity.role and AuditEvent.entity.detail.type rather than obsolete AuditEvent.entity.type wording. No generated or out-of-build artifacts were edited.
source_changes: source/auditevent/structuredefinition-AuditEvent.xml: added a valueBase64Binary-specific comment to AuditEvent.entity.detail.value[x] explaining that decoded content meaning and secondary encoding are event-specific and must be understood by consuming applications.

related_jiras.note: Expanded AuditEvent.entity.detail.value[x] datatypes and explains why the earlier FHIR-13759 detail-value comment disappeared; it did not repeal the base64Binary clarification.
